studies.description: In the Rodent Research Reference Mission (RRRM-2), forty female C57BL/6NTac mice were flown on the International Space Station. To assess differences in outcomes due to age, twenty 12 week-old and twenty 29 week-old mice were flown, respectively. To directly assess spaceflight effects, half of the young and old mice (10 old, 10 young) were sacrificed on-orbit after 55-58 days (ISS Terminal, ISS-T), while the other half (10 old, 10 young) were returned live to Earth after 32 days and allowed to recover for 24 days (Live Animal Return, LAR) before sacrifice. ISS-T and LAR mice were the same age at sacrifice. Both the ISS-T and LAR animals had independent ground controls (10 mice per group housed in flight hardware in matched environmental conditions), basal controls (10 mice per group sacrificed 2 days before launch), and vivarium controls (10 mice per group housed within standard vivarium habitats). Thus RRRM-2 included a total of 160 mice. This study includes bulk RNA sequencing and single nuclei transcriptomics and epigenomics from left cerebral hemispheres from 4 young ISS-T spaceflight animals, 5 old ISS-T spaceflight animals, 5 young ISS-T ground control animals, and 4 young ISS-T ground control animals.

protocols.description: In the Rodent Research Reference Mission (RRRM-2), forty female C57BL/6NTac mice were flown on the International Space Station. To assess differences in outcomes due to age, twenty 12 week-old and twenty 29 week-old mice were flown, respectively. To directly assess spaceflight effects, half of the young and old mice (10 old, 10 young) were sacrificed on-orbit after 55-58 days (ISS Terminal, ISS-T), while the other half (10 old, 10 young) were returned live to Earth after 32 days and allowed to recover for 24 days (Live Animal Return, LAR) before sacrifice. ISS-T and LAR mice were the same age at sacrifice. Both the ISS-T and LAR animals had independent ground controls (10 mice per group housed in flight hardware in matched environmental conditions), basal controls (10 mice per group sacrificed 2 days before launch), and vivarium controls (10 mice per group housed within standard vivarium habitats). Thus RRRM-2 included a total of 160 mice. GeneLab only processed up to 5 mice from each of the young/old group from flight/ground control groups in this dataset. All mice (C57BL/6NTac) were sourced from Taconic Biosciences (Germantown, NY). Mice were weighed, chipped with BMDS RFID chip (IMI-500) and shipped to NASA KSC for delivery at approximately L-5 weeks. Mice were housed and maintained in the Animal Care Facility (ACF) at NASA KSC with 12:12 light cycle matched in timing to the light cycle used for Transporters and Habitats programmed for flight. All mice were housed in cages of 5 mice/cage with the same littermates as they had been raised. Mice were initially given ad lib standard lab chow and water, which was changed on a schedule of 2x per week. Mice were housed initially on standard bedding and provided with igloo as enrichment material. Animal health was checked daily by appropriately trained NASA personnel and contracted lab technicians. At L-4 weeks, mice were placed on raised mesh flooring to simulate spaceflight Transporter and Habitat cage conditions, given water delivered through lixits identical to those used in the flight hardware and put on the NASA Nutrient-Upgraded Rodent Foodbars (NuRFB). Food and water were changed weekly, and mice were weighed bi-weekly. Igloo was provided as enrichment material in all cages. At L-12 days, mice were grouped (10 mice per cage) in larger cages for social acclimation prior to launch. Groupings were done based on age of animals and in a manner to establish similar average weights between any given grouping. At L-2 days, baseline, spaceflight and ground control groups were identified. At L-1 day, spaceflight animals were loaded into spaceflight Transporters. Habitat Ground Control (HGC) mice were loaded into Transporters on a 3-day offset from spaceflight animals. Vivarium Ground Control (VGC) mice (also on a 3-day offset) were returned to 5 mice/cage and placed on standard bedding and provided water through typical sipper tubes at launch equivalent. All mice were maintained on NuRFB throughout the duration of the study. Spaceflight and HGC mice were given new food at weekly intervals. VGC mice were given new food and fresh water also on weekly intervals. An enrichment Hut, in the form of a grated shelter, was provided in the habitat for the flight and habitat ground control group. Igloo was provided in the vivarium ground control group. After splashdown, flight LAR mice were transferred to the animal care facility at Scripps Research Institute where they were assessed and re-caged into standard caging conditions (5 mice/cage, standard bedding and ad lib water from regular sipper tubes). LAR and ISS-T Ground Control mice were shipped from Kennedy Space Center to Scripps and housed under the same conditions as the flight mice. The study followed recommendations in the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and the protocol was approved by the NASA Flight Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
protocols.name: Animal Husbandry

protocols.description: For ISS terminal (ISS-T) group, mice were anesthetized with ketamine/xylazine and euthanized by means of cardiac puncture blood draw (exsanguination) and double thoracotomy. A list of tissues including brain were dissected fresh from each carcass. The left brain hemisphere was dissected and placed directly in a cryotube and rapidly frozen using the ISS rapid freeze system. The samples were maintained at -80C until the day of nuclei isolation and nucleic acid extraction.
protocols.name: sample collection

protocols.description: On the day of nuclei isolation, the hemisphere was placed in a plastic weigh boat on a pre-cooled metal stage on dry ice and sectioned coronally using two cuts to generate a 30mg (+/-5mg) sized slice that included the region between sections 74 – 60 in Allen Brain Atlas (mouse, P56, coronal), without allowing the sample to thaw. The resulting slice encompassed areas of the hippocampus, ventricles, amygdala, hypothalamus, midbrain, and striatum. To isolate nuclei, Chromium Nuclei Isolation Kit with RNase Inhibitor (10X Genomics, Pleasanton, CA) was used. All buffers were kept on ice until needed. Up to 6 samples were processed at once. Approximately 30mg of brain tissue was isolated, using a cold blade, and immediately placed in 200uL of freshly made lysis buffer in tissue dissociation tubes set on ice. To dissociate the tissue, plastic pestle was used to grind through the tissue in the lysis buffer until homogeneous. 300uL of fresh lysis buffer was added to each sample and pipette mixed 10 times. All samples were incubated on ice for 10 minutes and then transferred into pre-chilled Nuclei Isolation Column assembled with Collection Tube. Samples were centrifuged at 16,000 rcf for 20 seconds at 4C. The columns were discarded, samples vortexed and then centrifuged again for 3 minutes at 500 rcf at 4C. Supernatant was carefully discarded. Pelleted nuclei were resuspended in 500uL of Debris Removal Buffer by gentle pipetting and the tubes were centrifuged at 700 rcf for 10 minutes at 4C. Supernatant was discarded and to wash the nuclei pellet, it was resuspended in 1mL of Wash Buffer and then centrifuged at 500 rcf for 5 minutes, supernatant discarded. Additional 1mL wash was performed and the supernatant discarded. Washed nuclei were resuspended in 150uL of Resuspension Buffer and kept on ice. To count the nuclei, 20uL of nuclei suspension was combined with 40uL of 4uM EthD-1 stain. Stained samples were incubated for 15-25 minutes and were evaluated and counted using a haemocytometer on a Leica DMi8 microscope with TXR fluorescent filter. Cell suspension volume corresponding to 6,000 nuclei was carried over into the 10X Chromium workflow. GeneLab only processed samples from 4 young ISS-T spaceflight animals, 5 old ISS-T spaceflight animals, 5 young ISS-T ground control animals, and 4 young ISS-T ground control animals.
protocols.name: Nucleus Isolation

protocols.description: 10X Genomics procedure for library preparation with Chromium Next GEM Single Cell Multiome ATAC + Gene Expression was followed (10X Genomics, Pleasanton, CA), since this kit can be used for either isolated nuclei or cells. Nuclei suspension was incubated in a Transposition Mix to fragment the DNA in open regions of the chromatin. Simultaneously, partial adapter sequences were added. Using the Chromium Controller (10X Genomics, Pleasanton, CA), the nuclei were encapsulated in Gel bead-in-Emulsion, or GEMs, with each GEM individually tagged with one of 750,000 independent 10X barcodes. Multiome ATAC+GEX Gel Beads include both a)Poly (dT) sequences that are associated with full length cDNA from poly-A mRNA for gene expression (GEX) and b)Spacer sequence that enables barcode attachment to transposed DNA fragments for ATAC-Seq library. Within the GEM’s, reverse transcriptase reaction took place and Illumina P5 sequence, 16nt 10X barcode (ATAC and GEX), Illumina TruSeq Read 1 sequencing primer, 12nt unique molecular identifier (UMI) and 30nt poly(dT) sequence all anneal to either the transposed DNA fragments or mRNA fragments that get transcribed to cDNA. Incubation in the GEM’s produces 10X barcoded DNA from transposed DNA (ATAC) and 10X barcoded, full length cDNA from poly-A mRNA (GEX). Following reverse transcription and barcoding, a quenching reaction took place and the GEMs were ruptured to release the content. Barcoded fragments were recovered and clean-up was conducted using DynaBeads MyOne Silane magnetic beads followed by SPRISelect (Beckman Coulter, Indianapolis, IN) clean up and size selection. Fragments were amplified to increase yield, 7 amplification cycles were completed using the provided reagents and the amplified product was cleaned and size selected by SPRISelect (Beckman Coulter, Indianapolis, IN) beads. Amplified product included transposed DNA fragments used for subsequent ATAC-Seq library preparation and barcoded cDNA fragments for gene expression library preparation. To complete the ATAC-Seq library construction, 40uL of each of the transposed DNA samples were combined with Sample Index PCR Mix that includes Illumina P7 sequence. Individual Sample Indexes from 10X plate N, Set A were also added to the PCR reaction. Fully barcoded and indexed libraries were amplified for 8 amplification cycles. ATAC-Seq library size selection and clean-up was conducted using SPRISelect (Beckman Coulter, Indianapolis, IN) beads. Sequencing libraries were quantified using Qubit 4 instrument (ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) with Qubit 1X dsDNA HS Assay (ThermoFisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter and library quality was assessed with TapeStation 4200 instrument (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) with D1000 or D1000 HS DNA ScreenTape Analysis assay. Library quality assessment was performed on iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Library Construction

protocols.description: RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Sequencing was set up as following: Read 1: 28 bp, Index 1: 10 bp, Index 2: 10 bp. Read 2: 91 bp. PhiX included as control and to increase library diversity. Protocol followed is SOP 7.1-Setting up NovaSeq 6000 and iSeq 100 Sequencers. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Sequencing - snRNAseq

protocols.description: Raw fastq files from each sample were assessed for % rRNA using HTStream SeqScreener (version 1.3.2) screened against a fasta file of Mus musculus rRNA sequences retrieved from NCBI on Sep-2021. Raw fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.11.9) and MultiQC (version 1.12) was used to generate MultiQC reports.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol - snRNAseq

protocols.description: DNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Sequencing was set up as following: Read 1: 51 bp, Index 1: 8 bp, Index 2: 24 bp, Read 2: 51 bp. PhiX included as control and to increase library diversity. Protocol followed is SOP 7.1-Setting up NovaSeq 6000 and iSeq 100 Sequencers. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs. Published data files reflect the following read lengths post processing: Read 1 (forward): 51 bp, Read 2 (10X barcode): 24 bp, Read 3 (reverse): 51 bp.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Sequencing - snATACseq

protocols.description: Raw fastq files for the 4 indices for each sample were concatenated together to create one set of fastq files per sample. Concatenated raw fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.11.9) and MultiQC (version 1.12) was used to generate MultiQC reports.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol - snATACseq

protocols.description: On the day of nucleic acid extraction, the left hemisphere was placed in a plastic weigh boat on a pre-cooled metal stage on dry ice and the frontal lobe of left hemisphere sectioned using cuts to generate a 20 mg sized tissue. All the sample processing were kept consistent, without allowing the sample to thaw. RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) following GeneLab SOP 3.1-Qiagen AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini with Qiagen RNase-Free DNase set. Homogenization buffer for RNA purification was made by adding 1:100 beta-mercaptoethanol to Buffer RLT (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) and kept on ice until use. Approximately 20 mg of tissue was isolated using a scalpel, weighed, and immediately placed in 700 µL of the Buffer RLT solution. Homogenization was performed using tissue homogenizing bead mix red, (Next Advance, Raymertown, NY) on Bullet Blender Gold 24 (Next Advance, Raymertown, NY) for 3 minutes at 4 ˚C per SOP 2.1-Tissue homogenization Using Bullet Blender Gold Bead Beater. Homogenates were centrifuged for 5 minutes at RT and 14,000 g to remove cell debris. The supernatant from each sample was then used to isolate and purify DNA and RNA following the manufacturer protocol. RNA was eluted in 50 µL RNAse free H2O, and DNA was eluted in 50 µL RNAse free H2O. Concentration for all RNA samples were measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA) with Qubit RNA BR kit following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with the Agilent RNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). DNA quality and size were assessed using the Agilent 4200 TapeStation with Agilent gDNA ScreenTape Kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). GeneLab only processed samples from 4 young ISS-T spaceflight animals, 5 old ISS-T spaceflight animals, 5 young ISS-T ground control animals, and 4 young ISS-T ground control animals. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Extraction

protocols.description: ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, Cat 4456739, v92), Mix 1 or Mix 2, were added on the day of library prep at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol. SOP 5.2 Use of ERCC Spike-In Mixes and UMRR/UHRR Controls for Total RNA Sequencing. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Spike-in Protocol

protocols.description: RNA ribo depletion and library preparation was done with Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep Gold (Illumina Inc., San Diego, CA) following GeneLab SOP 5.1 Ilumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Lirary Prep using epMotion. Input RNA were approximately 500 ng with RIN greater than 4. Index adapters used were at 1.5 µM (IDT, 384-well xGen Dual Index UMI Adapters). 15 cycles PCR were performed. Library fragment size was assessed using Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA) following GeneLab SOP 6.3 Quality analysis of sequencing libraries using 4200 TapeStation System with D1000 reagent kit. Pooled library concentration was measured by Qubit 4 Fluorometer (ThermoFisher Scentific, Waltham, MA) following SOP 4.1-RNA/DNA/miRNA/cDNA Quantification using Qubit Fluorimeter. Library quality assessment was performed on iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA). GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Library Construction - bulkRNAseq

protocols.description: RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Sequencing was set up as following: Read 1: 151 bp, Index1: 17 bp, Index2: 8 bp, Read 2: 151 bp. PhiX v3 was included as control and to increase library diversity. Protocol followed is SOP 7.1-Setting up NovaSeq 6000 and iSeq 100 Sequencers. GeneLab Sample Processing SOP can be found at the GitHub page, https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab-sampleProcessing/tree/master/SOP_docs.
protocols.name: Nucleic Acid Sequencing - bulkRNAseq

protocols.description: Unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) were incorporated into the read headers of raw fastq files using UMI-tools version 1.1.2. Raw fastq files from each sample were assessed for % rRNA using HTStream SeqScreener (version 1.3.2) screened against a fasta file of Mus musculus rRNA sequences retrieved from NCBI on May-2024. Raw fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1) and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Samples with total read pairs exceeding 150 million were downsampled to 150 million read pairs with seqtk (version 1.4-r122).
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol - bulkRNAseq

protocols.description: Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.0.1 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/tree/NF_RCP-2.0.1/RNAseq/Workflow_Documentation/NF_RCP). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), inner distance was assessed using RSeQC inner_distance.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to forward and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0), ERCC genes were removed, and the non-ERCC genes were normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1). Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
protocols.name: GeneLab RNAseq data processing protocol
